Future Present Labs
Technical preview

Linux for connected machines.

fungOS is a mesh-native stack: Mycelium gives every machine an identity, discovery, DNS and signed updates; Soil runs sandboxed Spores; Canvas is the workspace; Unibus moves events and media.

Install it on the macOS or Linux machine you already use, or boot the preview image in a VM.

Install in one line Preview images Documentation

Preview: fungOS Linux images are built and tested in QEMU; public images are not available yet. The Mycelium installer is available today for macOS and Linux.

Install in one line

One command installs Mycelium, Soil, the Canvas workspace and the bundled Spores on macOS or Linux. It does not reinstall the operating system.

curl -fsSL https://sh.fungos.dev/install.sh | bash -s --

Joining an existing fleet uses a short-lived code minted by the authority:

curl -fsSL https://sh.fungos.dev/install.sh | bash -s -- --code "MYC1-..."
Identity and mesh
Mycelium node identity, discovery, topology, mesh DNS and the iroh-tun IPv6 overlay.
Access
Short-lived SSH certificates, roles and per-host least-privilege grants.
Workspace
Soil runtime and Canvas: native windows, tiled workspaces and terminal sessions.
Spores
Sandboxed, capability-granted apps — terminal, files, browser — launched from the catalogue.
Updates
A signed release channel, health checks and rollback.

Once the 0.1.0 archives are public, add --release latest to skip the source build. The installer verifies the downloaded archive against the release checksums, then asks for sudo for the root tunnel and DNS services.

macOS, or a systemd Linux host. Full install notes.

Discover. Map. Enroll. Update.

Discovery
Find machines, services, network equipment and attached resources.
Topology
See sites, subnets, links and how devices connect.
Enrollment
Provisioned machines join on first boot using short-lived Mycelium claims.
Access
Manage peer identity, roles and SSH access.
Updates
Distribute signed software, check activation health and recover from failed updates.
Workspace
Canvas arranges native windows, terminals and Spores into named workspaces.
Apps
Spores run as sandboxed components with explicit capability grants.

Mycelium also runs independently on existing machines. You don’t need to reinstall a device to bring it into your fleet.

Checksums · Signature · Release public key · Test and license evidence

Verify your download

Confirm this release-key fingerprint through a separately trusted channel before admitting the downloaded key:

FC3C04696D437DCD2F51895F0BEFDC5CF68C7CBA

gpg --show-keys --with-fingerprint fungos-release-key.asc
gpg --dearmor --output fungos-release-keyring.gpg fungos-release-key.asc
gpgv --keyring ./fungos-release-keyring.gpg SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS

Download every listed file for a complete checksum check. On macOS, use shasum -a 256 --check SHA256SUMS. Torrent hashes alone do not authenticate a release. These torrents include HTTPS webseeds; no persistent public peer seeder is promised.

Start with the QEMU installation guide, or add Mycelium to an existing machine without reinstalling it.

  • Pi 3B+ · arm64 · headless edge
    Owner-personalized image. Filesystem checks passed; hardware boot pending.
  • Base / edge · amd64 and arm64
    Rootfs tarballs built and inspected. Not standalone boot images.
  • Cloud · amd64
    Rootfs verified with nested Firecracker in QEMU. Not a provider image.

Try the qualification installer in a disposable VM. Physical hardware, Pi and full edge images remain unreleased. This frozen build is not a security/compliance certification or a production-install recommendation.

Running fungOS

A rebuilt edge image enrolled, downloaded Unibus and Canvas through peers, and retained its identity and healthy services after reboot. Signed updates and rollback are separately verified.

The compositor remains manually updated until its display health check is ready.

About the project

fungOS is developed by Future Present Labs for homelabs, on-premises fleets, studios and compute nodes.

Mycelium manages machines. Unibus provides discovery and transport multiplexing across applications, devices and media. Canvas provides the interface. Shroud runs workloads. Each stands on its own.

  • Open source — first-party foundations target MIT / Apache-2.0.
  • Right to repair — modular drivers for mixed hardware.
  • Privacy — local operation and least-privilege access.
  • Interoperability — existing tools and native transports.

Upstream packages keep their own licenses. Standard and opt-in AGPL application selections are planned.

Join the fungOS Discord for project news, development, and community support.

Mycelium source · Future Present Labs

Security

Discovery does not grant access. People and machines have separate identities; roles control permitted actions. Images do not clone peer credentials.

No current image is certified for regulated or classified use. Security profiles and current limits.
